title: Adaptive batch-sampling and warmup policy for FlashAttention v3 integration
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Problem statement: After integrating FlashAttention v3 as a candidate kernel, we observed intermittent latency/regression on long-sequence prefill-heavy workloads. Root-cause signals point to two interacting phenomena: (1) cold-start sampling produces micro-batches that are suboptimal for v3's tiling heuristics, and (2) aggressive decode-prefill interleaving results in KV-cache pressure and kernel hotpath thrashing. Goal: implement an adaptive batch-sampling strategy plus a warmup policy that (a) steers early request streams toward stable kernel choices, (b) reduces prefill-induced kernel-switch churn, and (c) preserves throughput and tail latency constraints for latency-sensitive customers.
comments: 2025-02-13 — Aisha Patel: Collected initial traces from runtime-prod on long-chat workloads (seq 8k-16k). Noticed v3 performs well in steady-state but regresses during startup when sample batch sizes oscillate. Attached dashboard link.

2025-02-18 — Liam Chen: Prototype adaptive sampler implemented (sampler-v1): uses sequence-length histogram + recent kernel success rate to bias batch composition toward larger contiguous micro-batches when v3 is favored. Unit tests and microbenchmarks in perf harness show 6-9% throughput improvement over naive sampling on synthetic loads.

2025-02-20 — Design decision: prefer probabilistic sampling with decay window (30s) instead of deterministic sticky routing to avoid cold pinning errors. Trade-off: short-term suboptimality for improved long-term stability. Documented rationale in Confluence.

2025-02-24 — Integration: Added warmup policy that treats the first N prefills for a model variant as 'warmup' and forces conservative kernel (v2-like) selection until success_lift > 0.8. N is tunable per model and inferred from historical latency variance. Early experiments reduce 95th-ms spikes but slightly increase median latency for tiny requests.

2025-02-27 — QA: Ran canary across dedicated pool in us-west-2 for 48h against real traffic pattern (customer-sim). Observed elimination of multi-second start-of-session spikes for 75% of sessions. Found regression cases when batch skew is extreme (90% short, 10% very long)—sampler needs additional outlier handling.

2025-03-02 — Code review: PR #11347 submitted. Feedback from Marco Ruiz (runtime) to add metrics for kernel-switch frequency and prefill-decoder interleave ratio. Action: add two histograms and a counter before landing.

2025-03-03 — Liam Chen: Implemented metric hooks and toggles. Preparing rollout plan: staged canary -> 10% fleet -> 50% -> rollout. Include automatic rollback if kernel-switch freq spike > 2x baseline or 95th latency delta > 10% for two consecutive hours.
Follow-ups: tune decay window per model family, add learning job to propose N warmup length from historical traces, evaluate cost delta for embedding-heavy workloads.
